fields.sections.0.ko: Aligning text in monospace fonts to look good is more complex than it might seem. Left alignment is straightforward, but moving to right or center alignment requires counting spaces precisely, and fine-tuning such as half-spacing becomes impossible. Full justification worsens the situation, with irregular expansion of spaces between words making the text uncomfortable to read.
fields.sections.1.ko: In traditional typography, hyphenation has solved this problem by splitting words. But using hyphens in monospace fonts causes the hyphen character to draw excessive attention, and creates inconvenience when copying text. As a result, fully justified sentences are rarely found in text files.
fields.sections.2.ko: Yet one method remains: rewriting the text itself and carefully selecting words so that each line ends with exactly a predetermined number of characters. This way, the right edge of each line always ends with a character, and awkward double spaces do not appear.
fields.sections.3.ko: In the late 1990s, rs1n actually applied this technique when writing the Super Metroid guide. That guide, over 17,000 words in length, has perfectly aligned right margins on every line and contains not a single awkward double space. In the simple explanation "merely selected words carefully," the author revealed having performed all this work using only an ASCII editor.
fields.sections.4.ko: The author of this piece shares this case mainly as an interesting technical example. In physical book publishing, rewriting text to avoid unfavorable line breaks (widows, orphans) is common practice, but such adjustments are rare in online writing. Yet anyone with experience spending hours fitting button text or tooltip phrasing to a defined width in software interfaces would fully understand the obsessiveness and precision of this approach.
fields.caveat: This piece is a personal reflection on a particular aesthetic choice and the effort hidden behind it, so additional contextual information would be needed to assess the actual impact of the rs1n case on modern web design or accessibility.
